clue.text: Baked meats distributed by Saul's gaolers

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread about and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Food parcels handed out to prisoners by the jailers of a man called Saul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges SAULS and GAOLERS together; the apostrophe's S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry-wrapped sausage meat is baked, so these are savoury baked goods of meat.

clue.text: Race-official's first course

explanation.surface: A man who starts a race also serves the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A race official firing the gun starts the race; the opening dish of a meal is also so named.

clue.text: Release and remove head of BBC

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: Free the corporation's top man from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is a British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo knots and so set loose.

clue.text: What has succulent shoots and a well-inverted sugar?

parts.note: a spa is a well or spring

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A riddle about a plant and an upturned sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is grown for its tender edible spears.

clue.text: Section of knee bone found in a dark wood

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cut through a kneecap shows something dark like timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'found in', which is a link; the definition is just 'a dark wood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for ebony, a black hardwood.

clue.text: International contest requiring daily mop-out?

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Games so messy it needs mopping up each day.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympiad is a staging of the Olympic Games or an international academic competition.

clue.text: Mark of a son having left murder victim

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam, was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: Scar left on the son who was the first murder victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a son' points to Abel being Adam's son; L comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag or mark identifying something.

clue.text: End in action is minutely described

indicators.note: one piece is put in the middle of the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: Finishing a task is spelt out in fine detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Detailed means set out item by item, thoroughly.

clue.text: "The Silver King" is accepted by actor

indicators.note: being accepted means being taken inside the other word

parts.note: an agent is one who acts, an actor
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A performer takes on the role of a monarch in a play titled The Silver King.
explanation.walkthrough: The Silver King was a Victorian melodrama; 'The' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Argent is the heraldic term for silver.

clue.text: Opposed to false responses in church

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
phony means fake or false

explanation.surface: A protester objects to insincere replies given during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is alternate singing or chanting by two choirs answering each other in a service.

clue.text: Dim black king

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A gloomy monarch in mourning colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear as an adjective means bleary, misty or dull of sight.

clue.text: Not the practice of the circle line?

parts.note: the letter O is round like a circle
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A question about what a Tube route is like in principle rather than in use.
explanation.walkthrough: The circle line suggests London's Circle Line Underground route; here it gives O and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory is set against practice, as abstract principle versus actual doing.

clue.text: Fluid loss? The wise man will swallow something prescribed by the doctor

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one word goes into another

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a pill is a typical medical prescription

explanation.surface: An old sage takes his medicine and then suffers some leakage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillage is liquid lost by being spilt.

clue.text: Sack, the latest thing to clothe Virginia

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it round, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the rage is whatever is currently fashionable
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A sack dress is the newest fashion to dress a woman called Virginia in.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, to lay it waste.

clue.text: Vehicle cover for leaders of movement

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard is a protective cover

explanation.surface: A protective lorry escort for the heads of a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the foremost group in any movement, its pioneers.

clue.text: Hamlet with pages jumbled in small book

indicators.note: jumbled letters are mixed up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A copy of Shakespeare's play with its leaves shuffled out of order in a slim volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a thin unbound booklet.

clue.text: Book of Liam?

parts.note: the Daily Mail is a paper; written back to front it spells this name

explanation.surface: A question about a volume belonging to a man called Liam.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: take the paper (MAIL) back, giving LIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover edition is a kind of published volume.

clue.text: Bunthorne's bride, for example, has bluetits flying about

indicators.note: birds flying about are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bride in a story is surrounded by small fluttering birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunthorne's Bride is the second title of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative secondary title of a work, like that of Patience.

clue.text: This reptile is around in compound

indicators.note: a compound mixes elements together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A scaly creature is roaming about inside an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a pen; 'in compound' rearranges IS AROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinosaurs were prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: Preside over a disastrous court

parts.note: dire means dreadful or disastrous

explanation.surface: A judge has charge of a hearing that goes catastrophically.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct proceedings is to be in charge of them, chairing.

clue.text: Suit of spring design, cut off in the middle

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: cutting a word off halfway leaves its first half

explanation.surface: An outfit with a seasonal pattern, trimmed at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off in the middle' keeps DES, the first half of DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: For the rest of Hamlet, shut up!

explanation.surface: Telling someone to be quiet by quoting the prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's dying words are 'the rest is silence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls the rest beyond death this quiet state; also a command meaning be quiet.

clue.text: Obstruction in the course of a game

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a route is a course taken
let means hindrance, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A hurdle that crops up during a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Run over?

explanation.surface: Is someone knocked down by a car?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide, is an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run not off the bat is scored as such; also means surplus, left over.

clue.text: It sounds like the path of a woman on her wedding day

definitions.text: of a woman on her wedding day

indicators.note: this phrase announces that a word is to be said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a bridle path is a track for riders, so bridle stands for it

explanation.surface: A remark on the walk up the aisle that a bride takes.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path (bridleway) is a British track open to riders and walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is the adjective for things relating to a bride.

clue.text: Cooked food store's acquiring hard capital

indicators.note: acquiring takes a piece into the word

parts.note: a deli sells cooked meats and prepared food
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A delicatessen buying a tough commodity.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, as New Delhi, is the seat of India's government.

clue.text: Wear ornament

explanation.surface: Put on some decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to erode or wear away; a fret is also an angular repeating ornamental pattern.

clue.text: Weight of a girl's best china?

definitions.text: Weight of a girl's best china?

parts.words: Weight of a girl's best china?
parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate or friend (china plate), and diamonds are a girl's best friend, so this is the unit for weighing gems

explanation.surface: How heavy is a young woman's finest porcelain?
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' suggests crockery, but it is British rhyming slang: china plate = mate, i.e. friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemstones such as diamonds are weighed in this unit of 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Hearty epistoler wearing an oilskin hat

parts.note: a hearty is a sailor, as is a tar
St Paul wrote many of the New Testament epistles
in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: A jolly letter-writer sports a waterproof cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin was a sailor's tarred or waterproof hat.

clue.text: Constable's blade in peak fettle, it turns out

indicators.note: the letters turn out, appearing rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman's knife proves to be in excellent condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is the painter John Constable, not a policeman; 'it turns out' rearranges IN PEAK FETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter uses this flexible blade to mix or apply oil colours.
